text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/docs/implementation-plans/2026-09-30-standalone-timed-work-readiness.md\n+# Standalone timed LR/RC: additive implementation boundary\n+\n+Date: 2026-09-30\n+Status: Read-only architecture recommendation. No standalone SQL implementation, backend deployment, frontend switch or live standalone acceptance is claimed by this document. #166/#167 remain open.\n+\n+## Ship canonical manual sections first\n+\n+The smallest coherent expansion is a new account-owned sitting for one canonical LR or RC section selected from the already reviewed content manifest. It must preserve distinct retakes, enforce an acknowledged clock and reject stale or revoked writers on the server. Homework, classroom, bootcamp and custom timed pools require their own exact source contracts before entering this rollout. They remain explicitly identified legacy paths until that work passes; this partial expansion cannot close #167.\n+\n+Do not manufacture a one-leg PrepTest. The current deployed RPC accepts `workKind: practice-test`, creates a real `practice_test_runs` parent and freezes the full official leg definition. Altering its payload to represent a standalone section would misclassify Attempts, completion and score evidence.\n+\n+Current standalone LR already pauses on failed resume saves, but `drillResumeSession.ts` performs a raw `bootcamp_kv` UPSERT. Its write queue coordinates one JavaScript process, and `assertActiveTestLeg` only checks keys beginning `drill::practice-test::`. Manual section resume uses `drill::section::ptX-sY`, whose deterministic record identity is reused by retakes. RC already owns a UUID, but `RcPlayer.tsx` calls separate legacy session-clock, attempt and completion writes through `features/rc/api/rcProgress.ts`. Neither path acquires the deployed transactional PT authority.\n+\n+## Proposed additive server contract\n+\n+Names below are proposed, not installed capabilities.\n+\n+| Boundary | Required contract |\n+|---|---|\n+| `timed_section_configuration_v1` | Separate disabled-by-default rollout configuration, reviewed manifest hash and lease. Do not change enabled PT configuration. |\n+| `timed_section_sittings_v1` | UUID sitting ID; immutable owner, LR/RC kind, source kind/key, PT/section, ordered frozen queue, content hash, pace/budget and creation timestamp; mutable revision, epoch, device, phase and acknowledged elapsed/position under executor-only commands. |\n+| Active identity | Unique active `(owner, source_kind, source_key)` for supported canonical manual sections. Completed/abandoned sittings release the active slot and retain immutable history. Concurrent create returns the existing sitting or a defined conflict, never silently overwrites it. |\n+| Receipts | Dedicated append-only section receipts keyed by owner/sitting/command UUID, storing canonical envelope and committed revision. Exact replay returns its receipt plus current authority; changed-payload replay fails. Do not broaden the PT receipt constraint in place. |\n+| Source bindings | Immutable LR KV record identity and RC session UUID bound to the section sitting. LR uses a new per-sitting namespace, not the deterministic legacy key. Guard both OLD and NEW identities against rebinding or clearing protection. |\n+| Public RPCs | `timed_section_capability_v1`, `create_timed_section_v1`, `read_timed_section_v1`, `commit_timed_section_v1`. Commands: create, claim, start, checkpoint, heartbeat, pause, resume, close, abandon. No break/full-test advancement or scaled PT score. |\n+| Access | Authenticate the actor as the sitting owner; lock current applicable grants and validate exact frozen source before every command. Manual feature access must not be granted by an unrelated assignment. Completed result visibility and restricted question visibility are separate decisions. |\n+| Closeout | One transaction saves final answers, mandatory LR attempt/history/journal rows or RC session/attempt rows, analysis and terminal section state. A failure advances nothing; a retry creates no duplicate answers, history or completion timestamp. |\n+\n+Use a dedicated no-login/no-BYPASSRLS executor or a separately reviewed narrow extension of the existing executor. Ordinary authenticated writes must not reach protected controls or receipts. Adding another restrictive-looking permissive RLS policy does not override existing broad owner policies. Preserve existing PT guards and add section-aware enforcement without allowing identity-null or source-namespace escape. Scope any internal delegation to the reviewed function identity rather than a public user-settable flag.\n+\n+Freeze canonical content at creation using the selected manifest's exact section definition, including removed LR positions handled by the real normalizer and ordered RC passage/question IDs. Continue disclosing the existing client-derived correctness/analysis trust boundary; transactional save protection is not a new secure grading service.\n+\n+## Reuse these boundaries without calling PT RPCs for standalone work\n+\n+The deployed PT contract consists of `timed_practice_test_capability_v1`, `create_timed_practice_test_v1`, `read_timed_practice_test_v1` and `commit_timed_work_v1`. Supporting SQL includes `timed_pt_actor_v1`, `timed_pt_require_access_v1`, key validation, checkpoint/close-leg helpers, child guards, manifests, receipts and bindings. These functions consume `practice_test_runs`; their public behavior must remain unchanged. Reuse their algorithms and isolated race harness, not their PT parent as a section container. Check current live definitions before writing incremental SQL; do not replay the fresh-install writer artifact.\n+\n+`timedWorkClient.ts` currently validates a PT-only command and response shape. Extract shared durable-envelope, storage, receipt, error and Web Locks mechanics behind a generic internal transport while leaving its exported PT parser strict. Add a section-specific parser/adapter; do not weaken PT response validation to accept arbitrary objects. Reuse pure normalized-content parity and question panes from `timedLrAdapter.ts`, `timedRcAdapter.ts`, `timedChildController.ts` and `TimedOfficialChildRunner`, but remove assumptions about parent legs, break state and full-test navigation. Server lease accounting, bounded clock display, pending-command retention and account-switch generation guards apply unchanged.\n+\n+## Files and build order\n+\n+1. Add an incremental SQL proposal under `docs/implementation-plans/artifacts/`, dedicated section transaction verification under `scripts/verification/`, and fixtures covering both kinds. Read current schemas/policies first, including attempts ownership guard and RC session/attempt triggers.\n+2. Add section-specific transport/store and source selector under `src/lib/`. Extend manifest access without generating another divergent question catalog. Keep generated Supabase types untouched until actual deployed-schema regeneration.\n+3. Add a dedicated section runner route/page using official panes. Wire canonical manual launch from `src/pages/SectionDirections.tsx`, LR Practice launch and the RC canonical section launch only after capability confirmation. Inventory exact existing launch routes before editing them. Leave custom/assigned/bootcamp dispatch explicit and unchanged in this first batch.\n+4. Integrate owned section Attempts/Continue/Results/Review and first-answer history through `practiceSectionAttempts.ts`, `sectionHistory.ts`, the RC history adapters and shared student-scoped evidence. Distinguish these sittings from full PT rows; every action targets the same UUID. Teacher reads use the selected student; teacher practice creates the teacher's own sitting.\n+5. Retain existing saved LR/RC rows and ownerless browser copies. Present legacy reporting/resume policy clearly; no automatic adoption, historical rewriting or assignment completion backfill. New retakes require deliberate creation and preserve earlier terminal records.\n+\n+## Safe deployment and acceptance gates\n+\n+Before deployment, freeze counts and full sorted-row digests for all affected existing source tables, policy/function definitions and PT configuration. Install additive disabled schema/functions with bounded locks and a transaction that aborts if unrelated rows/policies change. Seed or reference the already reviewed catalog without replacing it. Confirm preservation after installation and before enabling only canonical manual sources. There is no destructive rollback; disable future section creation and forward-fix a defect while keeping existing results and pending receipts readable. Existing protected writers must have a documented recovery path while creation is disabled.\n+\n+Isolated PostgreSQL verification must include same-revision writes, concurrent create, save/takeover, save/revoke with real grant locks, lease expiry, terminal immutability, receipt replay after later revisions, changed-payload replay, transactional closeout failure, and every raw writer's OLD/NEW identity bypass. Verify ordinary HTTP JWT owner and foreign read/INSERT/UPDATE requests separately from simulated SQL-role tests. Retain all genuine QA records; never delete a probe fixture to make preservation appear clean.\n+\n+Browser gates for both LR and RC: failed hydration hides restricted questions; actual blocked answer/position/heartbeat save pauses clock/navigation; reload retains the exact pending envelope; retry acknowledges exactly once; a separately authenticated second context explicitly takes over and rejects the former writer; access revocation blocks subsequent writes while preserving results. A client-discarded response is not TCP lost-response proof. Exercise mandatory browser closeout and retake/History/Review links. Confirm phone, sidecar, laptop, wide and keyboard task walks before release.\n+\n+Report four states independently: implementation prepared, backend installed/enabled, frontend published, live acceptance verified. No state in this proposal substitutes for another. Existing full-PT physical-device, real lost-response, revoked in-flight and mandatory browser-closeout checks also remain open. Genuine Activity AI grading remains a separate possible-credit action requiring immediate confirmation. Deployment route authorization does not authorize that credit spend.\n*** End Patch"));

value=match[2];if((value.startsWith('\"')&&value.endsWith('\"'))||(value.startsWith(\"'\")&&value.endsWith(\"'\")))value=value.slice(1,-1);\n+ return[[match[1],value]];\n+}));\n+const credentialPath=process.argv[2];if(!credentialPath)throw new Error('Usage: standalone-timed-disabled-live.mjs <central-env-path>');\n+const credentials=parseEnv(await readFile(resolve(credentialPath),'utf8'));\n+const config=parseEnv(await readFile(resolve('.env'),'utf8'));\n+if(!config.VITE_SUPABASE_URL||!config.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY)throw new Error('Public app configuration unavailable');\n+const client=()=>createClient(config.VITE_SUPABASE_URL,config.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY,{auth:{persistSession:false,autoRefreshToken:false}});\n+const login=async prefix=>{\n+ const email=credentials[prefix+'_EMAIL'],password=[REDACTED];if(!email||!password)throw new Error('Required '+prefix+' credentials unavailable');\n+ const c=client();const r=await c.auth.signInWithPassword({email,password});if(r.error||!r.data.user)throw new Error(prefix+' authentication failed');\n+ return{client:c,id:r.data.user.id};\n+};\n+const student=await login('LSATPREP_TESTER'),teacher=await login('LSATPREP_ADMIN');\n+if(student.id===teacher.id)throw new Error('Distinct accounts required');\n+const role=await teacher.client.from('user_roles').select('role').eq('user_id',teacher.id);\n+if(role.error||!role.data?.some(r=>r.role==='admin'))throw new Error('Administrator role not acknowledged');\n+const checks={};\n+for(const[name,session]of[['student',student],['admin',teacher]]){\n+ const cap=await session.client.rpc('timed_section_capability_v1');\n+ checks[name+'EmptyOwnedRead_'+table]=!result.error&&Array.isArray(result.data)&&result.data.length===0;\n+ }\n+ const privateConfig=await session.client.from('timed_section_configuration_v1').select('enabled').limit(1);\n+ checks[name+'PrivateConfigurationDenied']=privateConfig.error?.code==='42501';\n+ const unavailable=await session.client.rpc('read_timed_section_v1',{p_work_id:randomUUID()});\n+ checks[name+'UnavailableSittingDenied']=unavailable.error?.code==='PT401';\n+}\n+const anonymous=client();const anonymousCap=await anonymous.rpc('timed_section_capability_v1');\n+checks.anonymousCapabilityDenied=Boolean(anonymousCap.error);\n+const anonymousRead=await Read knowledge from `wiki/`, not `raw/`. Use the `obsidian` CLI (`search`, `backlinks`, `read`) for graph traversal (needs the Obsidian app open); flat file reads work without it. When saving deliverables to the vault, use `[[wiki-link]]` syntax and `UPPERCASE-HYPHENATED.md` naming.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nScripts (from `package.json`):\\r\\n\\r\\n- `npm run dev` — Vite dev server on port 8080\\r\\n- `npm run build` — production build\\r\\n- `npm run build:dev` — build with development mode flags\\r\\n- `npm run preview` — serve the built bundle\\r\\n- `npm run lint` — ESLint flat config (`eslint.config.js`)\\r\\n- `npm run test` — Vitest single run (runner wired, no specs exist yet)\\r\\n- `npm run test:watch` — Vitest watch mode\\r\\n- Single test file: `npx vitest run path/to/file.test.ts`\\r\\n\\r\\nPackage manager: **npm**. `package-lock.json` is canonical. A stray `bun.lock` / `bun.lockb` exists in the repo — ignore it, do not switch tooling.\\r\\n\\r\\n- `npm run typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`. Formatting is ESLint-only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Architecture (big picture)\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Routing** — React Router v6. Routes are registered in `src/App.tsx`, pages live in `src/pages/`. `/foyer` is the landing surface. Feature-gated pages are wrapped by `ProtectedRoute`.\\r\\n- **Auth + permissions** — Supabase Auth session plus Lovable Cloud Auth JWT fallback (`@lovable.dev/cloud-auth-js`). Per-feature access flags (`has_practice_access`, `has_drill_access`, `has_chat_access`, `is_admin`, ...) are resolved in `src/hooks/useUserPermissions.ts`. Session death is detected via JWT/401.\\r\\n- **Supabase integration** — client auto-generated at `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts` (Supabase JS v2). DB types are auto-generated — do not hand-edit. SQL migrations in `supabase/migrations/`.\\r\\n- **State** — React Context for cross-cutting concerns (`AuthContext`, `UserSettingsContext`, `QuestionBankContext`, `ThemeContext`, `TimerContext`). TanStack Query v5 for server state.\\r\\n- **Primary navigation — Foyer** — `src/pages/AcademyFoyer.tsx` composes `src/components/foyer/FoyerSidebar.tsx` (state blocks + workspace nav) with `src/components/foyer/FoyerHeroRing.tsx` (3 nodes: Smart Drill, Resume, Ask Joshua). This is the primary nav for the product.\\r\\n- **Messaging / Inbox** — real messaging feature, not cosmetic. Core logic in `src/lib/`: `adaptiveEngine`, `drillIntelligence`, `achievementEngine`, `gamification`, `questionLoader`, `streakSystem`, `wajService`.\\r\\n- **Admin** — `AdminDashboard` + `admin-manage-users` edge function. Must be desktop AND mobile responsive. Needs granular per-feature toggle control.\\r\\n- **UI primitives** — shadcn/ui (Radix + `class-variance-authority`) in `src/components/ui/`. Icons from `lucide-react` and `@tabler/icons-react`. Framer Motion for animation. Spline for 3D.\\r\\n- **Styling** — Tailwind 3.4 over HSL custom properties in `src/index.css`, surfaced as tokens in `tailwind.config.ts`. `DESIGN.md` is the visual authority; `.impeccable/design.json` is its machine-readable sidecar. Prefer tokens over ad-hoc hex values, and never add a token name whose CSS variable is not defined - three such names (`accent-bronze`, `accent-warm`, `glow-bronze`) shipped broken for five months and silently removed the focus ring from every shared Button.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Conventions\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Git workflow:** Always commit and push directly to `main`. Never create feature branches or pull requests unless explicitly asked. After completing any code change: stage relevant files, commit with a descriptive message, and push to `main`.\\r\\n- **Push via `.claude/safe-push.sh`, not raw `git push`.** Lovable auto-commits to `main` mid-session; a raw push can get rejected or race a concurrent commit. The script fetches, merges origin/main if it diverged (never rebases, never force-pushes), then pushes.\\r\\n- **Never roll `main` back.** Do not use Lovable\'s \\"Revert to commit\\", \\"revert and resend\\", or history restore, and never reset or force-push `main`. On 2026-09-27 an accidental \\"revert and resend\\" (b998596) silently undid three merged PRs across 121 question-bank files, and students saw the wrong questions again. '{"chunk_id":"cfad34","wall_time_seconds":0.6300099,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1482,"output":"/**\\r\\n * Real RC sections, derived from the passage index.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * A **Section** here is what the test calls one: the four passages that appeared\\r\\n * together in one section of one PrepTest, in their published order. It is not a\\r\\n * drill you assemble — the composition is fixed, which is the whole point of\\r\\n * sitting one.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * Nothing new is stored. A section is expressed through the existing\\r\\n * `/rc?passages=…` link contract, and its clock through the existing\\r\\n * per-passage budget: `RC_STANDARD_SECONDS_PER_PASSAGE` (525s) across four\\r\\n * passages is 2100s — exactly the 35:00 a real section runs.\\r\\n */\\r\\nimport {\\r\\n  RC_STANDARD_SECONDS_PER_PASSAGE,\\r\\n  type RcIndexPassage,\\r\\n  type RcRevealMode,\\r\\n} from \'./rcTypes\';\\r\\n\\r\\nexport type RcIndexPassageWithPt = RcIndexPassage & { preptest: number };\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Every RC section on the modern test has exactly four passages. */\\r\\nexport const RC_SECTION_PASSAGE_COUNT = 4;\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * A real RC section carries 26-28 questions. That is a fact about the test, not\\r\\n * about our bank — so a section below it is *short*, and saying so is the only\\r\\n * honest way to offer one. Sections fall short because the source publishes\\r\\n * answer choices only for questions carrying a written explanation, and the rest\\r\\n * cannot be rendered or drilled. Never pad a section to hit this number.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport const RC_FULL_SECTION_MIN_QUESTIONS = 26;\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * Standard section timing, and the accommodations multiples of it.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * The labels are spelled the way the rest of the app spells them: \\"Time and a\\r\\n * half\\", not \\"Time & a Half\\". Nothing renders this list today, so the wording\\r\\n * was free to drift, and it had: the Testing Centre and the section door were\\r\\n * reconciled on the spelled-out sentence-case form and this was the last copy\\r\\n * still carrying the old one, waiting to reintroduce the inconsistency the\\r\\n * moment something wired it up.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport const RC_SECTION_PACES = [\\r\\n  { id: \'standard\', label: \'Standard\', secondsPerPassage: RC_STANDARD_SECONDS_PER_PASSAGE },\\r\\n  { id: \'time-and-a-half\', label: \'Time and a half\', secondsPerPassage: Math.round(RC_STANDARD_SECONDS_PER_PASSAGE * 1.5) },\\r\\n  { id: \'double-time\', label: \'Double time\', secondsPerPassage: RC_STANDARD_SECONDS_PER_PASSAGE * 2 },\\r\\n  { id: \'untimed\', label: \'Untimed\', secondsPerPassage: null },\\r\\n] as const;\\r\\n\\r\\nexport type RcSectionPaceId = (typeof RC_SECTION_PACES)[number][\'id\'];\\r\\n\\r\\nexport interface RcSection {\\r\\n  preptest: number;\\r\\n  section: number;\\r\\n  /** Passage ids in published order (Position 1-4). */\\r\\n  passageIds: number[];\\r\\n  passageCount: number;\\r\\n  /** Drillable questions across the whole section. */\\r\\n  questionCount: number;\\r\\n  /** True when the section carries a real section\'s worth of questions. */\\r\\n  fullLength: boolean;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * Group the index into sections, keeping only those a student can actually sit.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * A section with a passage that has no drillable questions is **excluded**, not\\r\\n * offered with a gap: reading three passages and answering questions on two is\\r\\n * not a section, and presenting it as one would misreport the student\'s pacing\\r\\n * more than it would help them. Three groups in the current bank are dropped by\\r\\n * this rule.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport function buildRcSections(passages: RcIndexPassageWithPt[]): RcSection[] {\\r\\n  const groups = new Map<string, RcIndexPassageWithPt[]>();\\r\\n  for (const p of passages) {\\r\\n    const key = `${p.preptest}:${p.section}`;\\r\\n    const list = groups.get(key);\\r\\n    if (list) list.push(p);\\r\\n    else groups.set(key, [p]);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n\\r\\n  const sections: RcSection[] = [];\\r\\n  for (const group of groups.values()) {\\r\\n    if (group.length !== RC_SECTION_PASSAGE_COUNT) continue;\\r\\n    if (group.some((p) => p.questionCount <= 0)) continue;\\r\\n\\r\\n    const ordered = [...group].sort((a, b) => a.setNumber - b.setNumber);\\r\\n    const questionCount = ordered.reduce((n, p) => n + p.questionCount, 0);\\r\\n\\r\\n    sections.push({\\r\\n      preptest: ordered[0].preptest,\\r\\n      section: ordered[0].section,\\r\\n      passageIds: ordered.map((p) => p.passageId),\\r\\n      passageCount: ordered.length,\\r\\n      questionCount,\\r\\n      fullLength: questionCount >= RC_FULL_SECTION_MIN_QUESTIONS,\\r\\n    });\\r\\n  }\\r\\n\\r\\n  return sections.sort((a, b) => a.preptest - b.preptest || a.section - b.section);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function rcSectionsForPreptest(sections: RcSection[], preptest: number): RcSection[] {\\r\\n  return sections.filter((s) => s.preptest === preptest);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function rcSectionPreptests(sections: RcSection[]): number[] {\\r\\n  return [...new Set(sections.map((s) => s.preptest))].sort((a, b) => a - b);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function rcSectionPace(id: RcSectionPaceId) {\\r\\n  return RC_SECTION_PACES.find((p) => p.id === id) ?? RC_SECTION_PACES[0];\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Total clock for a section at a given pace, in seconds. Null when untimed. */\\r\\nexport function rcSectionTotalSeconds(\\r\\n  section: RcSection,\\r\\n  paceId: RcSectionPaceId,\\r\\n): number | null {\\r\\n  const pace = rcSectionPace(paceId);\\r\\n  return pace.secondsPerPassage === null ? null : pace.secondsPerPassage * section.passageCount;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * The link that starts a section. Uses the existing hub contract, so an\\r\\n * assignment link and a student-started section are the same thing — and\\r\\n * `end_of_set` because a section is sat under test conditions, with review\\r\\n * afterwards rather than between passages.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport function rcSectionHref(\\r\\n  section: RcSection,\\r\\n  paceId: RcSectionPaceId = \'standard\',\\r\\n  reveal: RcRevealMode = \'end_of_set\',\\r\\n): string {\\r\\n  const pace = rcSectionPace(paceId);\\r\\n  const params = new URLSearchParams({\\r\\n    passages: section.passageIds.join(\',\'),\\r\\n    reveal,\\r\\n    timing: pace.secondsPerPassage === null ? \'untimed\' : \'standard\',\\r\\n    start: \'1\',\\r\\n    timedSection: \'manual-canonical\',\\r\\n  });\\r\\n  // Only the non-default paces need to say so; a plain `standard` link stays\\r\\n  // readable and keeps working on any build that predates this parameter.\\r\\n"}'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"c13cee","wall_time_seconds":0.3838395,"exit_code":1,"original_token_count":29,"output":"rg: scripts/knowledge/*.test.ts: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect. The real test breaks after two. */\\r\\n  breakAfterLeg: number;\\r\\n  /** True once the student has taken (or skipped) the break. */\\r\\n  breakTaken: boolean;\\r\\n  /** ISO stamp set when the break clock started, so it survives a reload. */\\r\\n  breakStartedAt?: string;\\r\\n  /** Device backup of the clock at a failed break exit. Never a running clock. */\\r\\n  breakRemainingSeconds?: number;\\r\\n  status: PracticeTestStatus;\\r\\n  createdAt: string;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Earlier PT118 sittings included experimental S3 and an extra S1 item. */\\r\\nexport function hasOutdatedPt118Structure(run: PracticeTestRun): boolean {\\r\\n  if (run.pt !== 118) return false;\\r\\n  const legs = run.legs.map((leg) => `${leg.kind}:${leg.section}:${leg.questionCount}`);\\r\\n  return legs.join(\',\') !== \'lr:1:25,rc:2:27,lr:4:25\';\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function practiceTestBreakRemainingSeconds(run: PracticeTestRun, now = Date.now()): number {\\r\\n  if (run.breakRemainingSeconds !== undefined) return run.breakRemainingSeconds;\\r\\n  if (!run.breakStartedAt) return PRACTICE_TEST_BREAK_SECONDS;\\r\\n  return Math.max(0, PRACTICE_TEST_BREAK_SECONDS - (now - Date.parse(run.breakStartedAt)) / 1000);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** A failed start or heartbeat resumes only after an account-acknowledged retry. */\\r\\nexport function retryPracticeTestBreakSave(accountRun: PracticeTestRun, pendingRun: PracticeTestRun, now = Date.now()): PracticeTestRun {\\r\\n  if (pendingRun.breakTaken) return pendingRun;\\r\\n  if (!accountRun.breakStartedAt && pendingRun.breakStartedAt) {\\r\\n    return { ...pendingRun, breakStartedAt: new Date(now).toISOString() };\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  if (pendingRun.breakRemainingSeconds !== undefined) {\\r\\n    const elapsed = PRACTICE_TEST_BREAK_SECONDS - pendingRun.breakRemainingSeconds;\\r\\n    return { ...pendingRun, breakStartedAt: new Date(now - elapsed * 1000).toISOString() };\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  return pendingRun;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** A heartbeat writes a clock snapshot to the device backup before account save. */\\r\\nexport function checkpointPracticeTestBreak(run: PracticeTestRun, now = Date.now()): PracticeTestRun {\\r\\n  return { ...run, breakRemainingSeconds: practiceTestBreakRemainingSeconds(run, now) };\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Keep the remaining time in the pending device copy while an exit save is unacknowledged. */\\r\\nexport function finishPracticeTestBreak(run: PracticeTestRun, now = Date.now()): PracticeTestRun {\\r\\n  return {\\r\\n    ...run,\\r\\n    breakTaken: true,\\r\\n    breakRemainingSeconds: practiceTestBreakRemainingSeconds(run, now),\\r\\n    breakStartedAt: undefined,\\r\\n  };\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport interface PracticeTestBlueprint {\\r\\n  pt: number;\\r\\n  legs: Omit<PracticeTestLeg, \'startedAt\' | \'completedAt\' | \'correct\' | \'answered\' | \'timeMs\'>[];\\r\\n  questionCount: number;\\r\\n  /**\\r\\n   * False when the Reading Comprehension leg carries fewer questions than a\\r\\n   * real section does. It does NOT require the RC section to carry a real\\r\\n * section\'s worth of questions, and that is a deliberate reversal: gating on\\r\\n * question count left 11 of 58 PrepTests sittable, because the bank publishes\\r\\n * only the RC questions that carry a written explanation.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * Refusing on those grounds was the wrong trade. An RC section\'s clock is a\\r\\n * reading budget — four passages at 8:45 each, whatever the question count —\\r\\n * so a section short a few questions still trains the thing the section\\r\\n * measures. What it changes is the raw total, and the raw total is stated\\r\\n * everywhere it matters rather than hidden.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * Still excluded: a section whose passages are not all present, or where a\\r\\n * passage carries no answerable questions at all. Reading a passage you cannot\\r\\n * be asked about is not practice, it is padding.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * Where a PrepTest carries a third LR section, use the lowest-numbered two\\r\\n * unless the official key identifies the experimental section. Section number breaks the tie, so\\r\\n    // the choice is stable across builds.\\r\\n    const existing = rcByPt.get(s.preptest);\\r\\n    if (\\r\\n      !existing ||\\r\\n      s.questionCount > existing.questionCount ||\\r\\n      (s.questionCount === existing.questionCount && s.section < existing.section)\\r\\n    ) {\\r\\n      rcByPt.set(s.preptest, s);\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n\\r\\n  const tests: PracticeTestBlueprint[] = [];\\r\\n  for (const [pt, lrList] of lrByPt) {\\r\\n    const rc = rcByPt.get(pt);\\r\\n    if (!rc) continue;\\r\\n    const lr = [...lrList].sort((a, b) => a.section - b.section).slice(0, 2);\\r\\n    if (lr.length < 2) continue;\\r\\n\\r\\n    const legs: PracticeTestBlueprint[\'legs\'] = [\\r\\n      ...lr.map((s) => ({ kind: \'lr\' as const, section: s.section, questionCount: s.count })),\\r\\n      {\\r\\n        kind: \'rc\' as const,\\r\\n        section: rc.section,\\r\\n        questionCount: rc.questionCount,\\r\\n        passageIds: rc.passageIds,\\r\\n      },\\r\\n    ].sort((a, b) => a.section - b.section);\\r\\n\\r\\n    tests.push({\\r\\n      pt,\\r\\n      legs,\\r\\n      questionCount: legs.reduce((n, l) => n + l.questionCount, 0),\\r\\n      rcFullLength: rc.fullLength,\\r\\n    });\\r\\n  }\\r\\n\\r\\n  return tests.sort((a, b) => a.pt - b.pt);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * Raw score to an estimated scaled score.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * These anchors describe a *typical* modern three-section LSAT curve, not this\\r\\n * PrepTest\'s official conversion table — we do not hold those. - Preserve all PT functions, configuration, manifests and existing sitting snapshots.

Existing controller, client, clock and closeout contracts can remain unchanged. No source or backend mutations were made.

Never regenerate the scored PrepTest catalog here.\n+import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';\n+import { readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';\n+import { resolve } from 'node:path';\n+import { buildTimedManifest, canonicalJson } from './build-timed-manifest';\n+import { normalizeQType } from '../../src/lib/questionLoader';\n+\n+const hash = (value: string | Buffer) => createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex');\n+const ensure = (value: unknown, message: string) => { if (!value) throw new Error(message); };\n+type Definition = { kind: 'lr' | 'rc'; section: number; questionCount: number; qids: string[]; questions: Record<string, unknown>[]; passageIds?: number[]; passages?: Record<string, unknown>[] };\n+export function buildStandaloneSectionManifest(root: string) {\n+  // Existing validation checks every raw LR/RC file and exact RC index membership,\n+  // including sources omitted from the scored three-leg selection.\n+  const validated = buildTimedManifest(root);\n+  const sections: { pt: number; definition: Definition }[] = [];\n+  for (const filename of readdirSync(resolve(root, 'public/data')).filter(name => /^PT\\d+-S\\d+-LR\\.json$/.test(name))) {\n+    const [, ptText, sectionText] = /^PT(\\d+)-S(\\d+)-LR\\.json$/.exec(filename)!;\n+    const pt = Number(ptText); const section = Number(sectionText);\n+    const rows = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, `public/data/${filename}`), 'utf8'));\n+    const questions = rows.filter(row => row.status !== 'removed').sort((a,b) => a.questionNumber-b.questionNumber).map(row => ({\n+      qid: `PT${pt}-S${section}-Q${row.questionNumber}`, qnum: row.questionNumber,\n+      qtype: normalizeQType(row.questionType || '', row.questionStem), level: row.questionDifficulty || row.Question_Difficulty || 3,\n+      contentSha256: hash(canonicalJson({stimulus: row.stimulus ?? '', stem: row.questionStem, choices: row.answerChoices})),\n+    }));\n+    sections.push({pt, definition:{kind:'lr',section,questionCount:questions.length,qids:questions.map(q=>q.qid),questions}});\n+  }\n+  const index = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'public/data/rc/rc-index.json'),'utf8'));\n+  for (const test of index.preptests) {\n+    const full = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, `public/data/rc/RC-PT${test.preptest}.json`),'utf8'));\n+    const sectionNumbers = [...new Set<number>(test.passages.map(p=>p.section))].sort((a,b)=>a-b);\n+    for (const section of sectionNumbers) {\n+      const passages = full.passages.filter(p=>p.section===section).sort((a,b)=>a.setNumber-b.setNumber);\n+      ensure(passages.length===4 && new Set(passages.map(p=>p.setNumber)).size===4, `Incomplete RC section ${test.preptest}:${section}`);\n+      const questions = passages.flatMap(p=>[...p.questions].sort((a,b)=>a.position-b.position).map(q=>({\n+        qid:String(q.questionId),questionId:q.questionId,passageId:p.passageId,qnum:q.position,\n+        contentSha256:hash(canonicalJson({text:p.text,prompt:q.prompt,choices:q.choices.map(c=>({letter:c.letter,text:c.text})).sort((a,b)=>a.letter.localeCompare(b.letter))})),\n+      })));\n+      sections.push({pt:test.preptest,definition:{kind:'rc',section,questionCount:questions.length,qids:questions.map(q=>q.qid),questions,\n+        passageIds:passages.map(p=>p.passageId),passages:passages.map(p=>({passageId:p.passageId,section:p.section,setNumber:p.setNumber,contentSha256:hash(p.text)}))}});\n+    }\n+  }\n+  sections.sort((a,b)=>a.pt-b.pt||a.definition.section-b.definition.section);\n+  ensure(sections.length===236 && sections.filter(s=>s.definition.kind==='lr').length===156, 'Canonical inventory changed; review required');\n+  for(let pt=101;pt<=159;pt++) ensure(sections.filter(s=>s.pt===pt).length===4, `Expected four bank sections for PT${pt}`);\n+  const identities = new Set(sections.map(s=>`${s.pt}:${s.definition.section}`));\n+  ensure(identities.size===sections.length,'Duplicate section identity');\n+  const deployed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root,'docs/implementation-plans/artifacts/timed-content-manifest-v1.generated.json'),'utf8'));\n+  for (const test of deployed.blueprints) for(const leg of test.legs) {\n+    const standalone = sections.find(s=>s.pt===test.pt && s.definition.section===leg.section && s.definition.kind===leg.kind);\n+    ensure(standalone && canonicalJson(standalone.definition)===canonicalJson(leg), `Deployed frozen definition mismatch PT${test.pt} ${leg.kind} S${leg.section}`);\n+  }\n+  const provenance = [...validated.provenance,{path:'scripts/knowledge/build-standalone-section-manifest.ts',sha256:hash(readFileSync(resolve(root,'scripts/knowledge/build-standalone-section-manifest.ts')))}].sort((a,b)=>a.path.localeCompare(b.path));\n+  for (const source of provenance) ensure(hash(readFileSync(resolve(root,source.path)))===source.sha256,`Source changed during generation: ${source.path}`);\n+  const body={schemaVersion:1,workKind:'standalone-section',provenance,sections};\n+  return {...body,manifestSha256:hash(canonicalJson(body))};\n+}\n+export function standaloneSeedSql(manifest: ReturnType<typeof buildStandaloneSectionManifest>) {\n+  return '-- Generated immutable standalone bank catalog. text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/docs/implementation-plans/artifacts/2026-09-30-standalone-catalog-upgrade-readiness.md\n+# All 236 standalone bank sections are prepared for a separate catalog\n+\n+Prepared on 2026-09-30. Managed installation and activation remain parent-owned.\n+\n+The canonical bank contains 156 LR and 80 RC sections across PT101–159. The scored three-leg PrepTest catalog covers 118 LR and 59 RC sections. The new standalone catalog adds the remaining 38 LR and 21 RC sections without changing the scored PrepTest selection. These omitted sections are not collectively labeled experimental.\n+\n+The generator validates raw LR rows, all RC passage files and their exact index memberships before producing the catalog. All 177 previously supported frozen definitions match the existing deployed artifact exactly. Removed LR questions stay excluded; original question numbers and canonical IDs stay intact. PT118 S3 retains its missing Q22 while its 24 served report positions remain dense.\n+\n+The immutable catalog hash is `714b27008d5c301c660d830d59562cc69814d06baae9d1e767240bece48b0c95`. The new generator and outputs have separate `all-sections-v2` names. Existing `build-timed-manifest.ts` and `timed-content-manifest-v1` artifacts were not changed.\n+\n+The upgrade copies every installed PrepTest catalog version into a separate `timed_section_content_manifests_v1` table. It validates the new four-column sitting FK before removing the old two-column FK. Only the standalone creation lookup and insertion guard lookup change. Existing sitting hashes, frozen definitions, question rosters, clocks, leases, bindings, receipts and child records are retained. The full PrepTest functions, configuration and original catalog remain unchanged.\n+\n+Installation does not select the new hash or change the enabled bit. After installation, old standalone creation still uses the previously selected catalog. Existing old sittings can resume and replay their exact receipts even after a later standalone-only catalog selection change.\n+\n+The prepared preserving wrapper measures and locks 21 live tables inside the same transaction: the original 18 PT/standalone/native tables plus Review episodes, Review events and native LR attempts. It compares original column values, row counts and duplicate-sensitive digests before commit. The read-only preflight and post-install artifacts also compare existing function definitions/ACL, policies, executor memberships and schema ACL, and disclose selected configurations.\n+\n+Verification passed 473 assertions in PGlite and real PostgreSQL 17. The real run used a non-superuser migration role with a different session user, retained its effective role and exact membership options, and verified an ordinary authenticated login cannot assume the executor or insert catalog content. Tests include two preexisting paused LR/RC sittings, old replay/resume after a test-only catalog switch, omitted LR/RC atomic closeout, immutable seed replay, and rollback of conflicting immutable content. Diagnostic databases were retained; no managed backend was touched.\n+\n+The install-only combined SQL is prepared in the machine's temporary directory with SHA256 `144c82e15fba4d08ac5345acecad02167ea99290aa0883a33abe1ce9c3a426cc` and 1,181,125 bytes. Before managed installation, the parent must obtain a fresh preflight snapshot, confirm the new table name is unused, and finish independent review. The wrapper itself measures current rows, so fresh QA answers and Review records are included automatically.\n+\n+After installation, compare the post-install preservation snapshot with the preflight snapshot. Only `standaloneCatalogExists` changes. Expect the new catalog to contain exactly 236 sections, all old definitions to be copied, every existing sitting to match its frozen definition, and ordinary/executor catalog inserts to be unavailable. Activation, frontend coverage expansion and real browser checks of newly supported LR/RC sections remain separate gates. No Edge Function deployment or Lovable credits are required by this preparation.\n*** End Patch"));

Install the schema first, then load\n+// immutable content in bounded, independently atomic and idempotent batches.\n+import {readFile,writeFile,mkdir} from 'node:fs/promises';\n+import {createHash} from 'node:crypto';\n+import {resolve} from 'node:path';\n+import {preservingDeployment} from './build-preserving-deployment.mjs';\n+const directory=resolve('docs/implementation-plans/artifacts');\n+const tables=['practice_test_runs','attempts','bootcamp_kv','section_history','rc_drill_sessions','rc_attempts','wrong_answer_journal','profiles','user_roles','practice_test_assignments','timed_pt_configuration_v1','timed_content_manifests_v1','timed_pt_receipts_v1','timed_pt_lr_bindings_v1','timed_section_configuration_v1','timed_section_sittings_v1','timed_section_receipts_v1','timed_section_source_bindings_v1','review_episodes_v1','review_episode_events_v1','intro_lr_attempts'];\n+const seed=await readFile(resolve(directory,'timed-section-all-sections-v2.generated.sql'),'utf8');\n+const statements=seed.match(/do \\$catalog\\$[\\s\\S]*?end \\$catalog\\$;/g);\n+if(!statements||statements.length!==236)throw new Error('Expected all236 immutable seed statements');\n+const body=seed.replace(/^--[^\\n]*\\nbegin;\\n/,'').replace(/\\ncommit;\\n$/,'');\n+if(statements.join('\\n')!==body)throw new Error('Full seed statement parity failed');\n+const batches=[];let pending=[];\n+const header='-- Bounded immutable standalone seed. text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/scripts/verification/standalone-catalog-readonly-live.mjs\n+// Ordinary JWT reads only. No creation/commit/configuration/source write RPCs.\n+import {readFile,writeFile} from 'node:fs/promises';\n+import {resolve} from 'node:path';\n+import {randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';\n+import {createClient} from '@supabase/supabase-js';\n+const parseEnv=text=>Object.fromEntries(text.split(/\\r?\\n/).flatMap(line=>{\n+ const match=line.match(/^\\s*([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\\s*=\\s*(.*?)\\s*$/);if(!match)return[];\n+ let value=match[2];if((value.startsWith('\"')&&value.endsWith('\"'))||(value.startsWith(\"'\")&&value.endsWith(\"'\")))value=value.slice(1,-1);\n+ return[[match[1],value]];\n+}));\n+if(!process.argv[2])throw new Error('Usage: standalone-catalog-readonly-live.mjs central-env-path [--output result-path]');\n+const secrets=parseEnv(await readFile(resolve(process.argv[2]),'utf8'));\n+const config=parseEnv(await readFile(resolve('.env'),'utf8'));\n+if(!config.VITE_SUPABASE_URL||!config.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY)throw new Error('Public app configuration unavailable');\n+const create=()=>createClient(config.VITE_SUPABASE_URL,config.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY,{auth:{persistSession:false,autoRefreshToken:false}});\n+async function login(prefix){\n+ if(!secrets[prefix+'_EMAIL']||!secrets[prefix+'_PASSWORD'])throw new Error(prefix+' credentials unavailable');\n+ const client=create();const response=await client.auth.signInWithPassword({email:secrets[prefix+'_EMAIL'],password:[REDACTED]});\n+ if(response.error||!response.data.user)throw new Error(prefix+' authentication failed');\n+ return{client,id:response.data.user.id};\n+}\n+const student=await login('LSATPREP_TESTER');const teacher=await login('LSATPREP_ADMIN');\n+if(student.id===teacher.id)throw new Error('Distinct fixture accounts required');\n+const checks={};const ownedCounts={};\n+async function snapshot(session,table){\n+ const order=table==='timed_section_receipts_v1'?'command_id':table==='timed_section_source_bindings_v1'?'sitting_id':'id';\n+ const response=await session.client.from(table).select('*').order(order);\n+ if(response.error||!Array.isArray(response.data))throw new Error('Owned '+table+' read failed');return response.data;\n+}\n+const tables=['timed_section_sittings_v1','timed_section_receipts_v1','timed_section_source_bindings_v1'];\n+let studentSitting;\n+for(const [name,session] of [['student',student],['admin',teacher]]){\n+ const before={};for(const table of tables)before[table]=await snapshot(session,table);\n+ const sittings=before.timed_section_sittings_v1;ownedCounts[name]=sittings.length;\n+ checks[name+'OwnedScope']=sittings.every(s=>s.owner_id===session.id);\n+ if(name==='student'){checks.studentExistingFixture=sittings.length>0;studentSitting=sittings[0]?.id;}\n+ const capability=await session.client.rpc('timed_section_capability_v1');\n+ checks[name+'EnabledCapability']=!capability.error&&capability.data?.contractVersion===1&&capability.data?.workKind==='standalone-section'&&capability.data?.enabled===true;\n+ checks[name+'ManualSource']=!capability.error&&JSON.stringify(capability.data?.sources)===JSON.stringify(['manual-canonical']);\n+ for(const sitting of sittings){\n+  const response=await session.client.rpc('read_timed_section_v1',{p_work_id:sitting.id});\n+  checks[name+'ExactRead_'+sitting.kind]=Boolean((checks[name+'ExactRead_'+sitting.kind]??true)&&!response.error&&JSON.stringify(response.data?.sitting)===JSON.stringify(sitting));\n+ }\n+ for(const table of ['timed_section_content_manifests_v1','timed_section_configuration_v1']){\n+  const response=await session.client.from(table).select('*').limit(1);\n+  checks[name+'Private_'+table]=response.error?.code==='42501'||(!response.error&&Array.isArray(response.data)&&response.data.length===0);\n+ }\n+ const missing=await session.client.rpc('read_timed_section_v1',{p_work_id:randomUUID()});checks[name+'MissingDenied']=missing.error?.code==='PT401';\n+ for(const table of tables)checks[name+'ReadPreserves_'+table]=JSON.stringify(await snapshot(session,table))===JSON.stringify(before[table]);\n+}\n+if(studentSitting){const foreign=await teacher.client.rpc('read_timed_section_v1',{p_work_id:studentSitting});checks.foreignSittingDenied=foreign.error?.code==='PT401';}\n+const anonymous=create();checks.anonymousCapabilityDenied=Boolean((await anonymous.rpc('timed_section_capability_v1')).error);\n+const output=JSON.stringify({checkedAt:new Date().toISOString(),ordinaryJwt:true,readOnly:true,recordsWritten:false,configurationChanged:false,\n+ scope:'ordinary capability and exact owned sitting read; catalog hash independently verified by managed read-only SQL',ownedCounts,checks},null,2);\n+if(process.argv.includes('--output'))await writeFile(resolve(process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--output')+1]),output+'\\n');\n+console.log(output);if(Object.values(checks).some(value=>!value))process.exitCode=1;\n*** End Patch"));

It is\\r\\n * listed here because the column is a plain string and every other format is,\\r\\n * not because the runner branches on it; the world does that.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport type ItemFormat = \\"free-text\\" | \\"mcq\\" | \\"variation\\" | \\"spoken-recall\\";\\r\\n\\r\\n/** One authored prompt within an Activity. */\\r\\nexport interface ActivityItem {\\r\\n  order: number;\\r\\n  /** The statement the student must respond to. */\\r\\n  prompt: string;\\r\\n  /** Author-supplied accepted answer(s); ground truth for the Coach. */\\r\\n  credited_answers: string[];\\r\\n  /** Why the credited answer is correct; revealed after the attempt cap. */\\r\\n  explanation: string;\\r\\n  /** Optional grouping label (e.g. \\"Universal Statement\\"). */\\r\\n  category?: string;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * One conceptual unit of a chunk, and the only thing completeness is measured\\r\\n * against.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * Written in plain analytic language, never in the stimulus\'s own wording. text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-ai-grading-integrity/docs/implementation-plans/2026-10-01-activity-ai-admission-readiness.md\n+# Activity coaching admission is prepared, disabled, and not deployed\n+\n+The additive migration `supabase/migrations/20261001120000_activity_ai_admission_v1.sql` creates private configuration, receipts, request aliases, and budget buckets. It changes no existing source schema or source records. Its configuration starts disabled. No provider calls, Lovable credits, or managed writes occurred in this preparation.\n+\n+## The server owns grading authority\n+\n+The Edge Function authenticates the actor and supplies that UUID to the service-only RPCs. Student-supplied UUIDs are never an authentication mechanism. Ordinary authenticated and anonymous callers have neither RPC execution nor table privileges. Even `service_role` has no direct privileges on these four tables; its only entry points are the three admission RPCs. Helpers are private, and table RLS has no permissive policies.\n+\n+Assignment admission requires the authenticated owner's nonrevoked assignment snapshot, a nonarchived canonical profile, an eligible assignment status, and exactly one matching item order. An issued assignment does not require `has_activity_access`. Preview requires both the owner's actual admin role and their authored Activity. Missing archive/revocation fields fail closed.\n+\n+The stored snapshot supplies the prompt, credited answers, explanation, category, coach, and optional authored checklist. Press checklists are derived from the snapshot explanation using the existing numbered-idea separators. The caller supplies only source identity, item order, response, attempt number, and request UUID. Response length is at most 10,000 characters and 40,000 UTF-8 bytes. Trusted content and result lengths are bounded too.\n+\n+Attempt two requires a completed trusted first receipt for the same canonical item and, for an assignment, a saved first response whose owner, source, item, attempt, response text, and verdict match that receipt. Student-authored history alone does not authorize answer-revealing second-attempt instructions. Preview uses its trusted first receipt because it has no assignment response history.\n+\n+## RPC envelopes used by the Edge Function\n+\n+`begin_activity_ai_request_v1(p_owner_id uuid, p_request_id uuid, p_source_kind text, p_source_id uuid, p_item_order integer, p_student_response text, p_attempt_no integer)` returns JSON with `ok`, `status`, `httpStatus`, `code`, `requestId`, and, when a receipt exists, `receiptId`.\n+\n+A `reserved` reply additionally has `claimId`, `leaseExpiresAt`, and `payload`. Payload fields are `statement`, `creditedAnswers`, `explanation`, `category`, `coach`, optional `ideas`, `studentResponse`, `attemptNo`, `sourceKind`, `sourceId`, `itemOrder`, and `firstAttemptConfirmed`. Nullable author fields remain null. A `cached` reply has `result` and does not debit quota.\n+\n+`dispatch_activity_ai_request_v1(p_owner_id uuid, p_request_id uuid, p_claim_id uuid)` returns `dispatched` exactly once for the reserved claim, with the same revalidated canonical `payload`. The Edge Function must observe this acknowledgment before its provider fetch. A repeated dispatch returns `in_flight` or `uncertain` and must not fetch again.\n+\n+`finish_activity_ai_request_v1(p_owner_id uuid, p_request_id uuid, p_claim_id uuid, p_result jsonb default null, p_failure_category text default null)` accepts a validated result or one failure category. Result keys are only `verdict`, `feedback`, and optional `covered`. Verdict is `correct`, `partial`, or `incorrect`; feedback is nonblank and at most 2,000 characters. Coverage numbers must belong to the trusted checklist; an empty array is retained. Valid result envelopes are stored exactly, so identical finish retries are replayable.\n+\n+Allowed failures are `provider_error`, `timeout`, `malformed_result`, `transport_error`, `cancelled`, `access_revoked`, `source_changed`, and `uncertain`. Root's Edge implementation maps gateway quota/credit rejections to `provider_error`, invalid model output to `malformed_result`, and ambiguous network/provider outcomes to `uncertain`. Failure codes and status values are semantic, with no raw source data or SQL exception details exposed by these replies.\n+\n+Typical denials are `invalid_request` / 422, `source_unavailable` / 403, UUID/content or claim conflicts / 409, `rate_limited` or `concurrency_limited` / 429, and `contract_disabled` / 503. Provider/result failures return 502. `in_flight` includes a bounded `retryAfterSeconds`; polling a receipt never authorizes another provider call.\n+\n+## Paid requests cannot silently repeat\n+\n+An existing request UUID binds an immutable canonical payload digest. Different UUIDs with the same owner and canonical request alias the same receipt. Global and actor advisory locks serialize admission and the budget checks. Initial defaults are 60 admissions per actor minute, 600 per actor UTC day, 6,000 globally per UTC day, and three active requests per actor. New reserved admissions debit all applicable buckets. Cache replay and reclaim of an expired, never-dispatched reservation do not debit again.\n+\n+Reservations expire after 30 seconds and can be reclaimed with a new claim. Dispatch renews the 30-second lease and changes state before the external fetch. Expired dispatched requests become uncertain, never reserved. Unknown outcomes remain part of concurrency, and only the original valid claim can finish them. A late validated response can resolve its own uncertain request. This deliberately favors stopping paid retries over guessing that a fetch never happened.\n+\n+Admission, dispatch, and successful finish all revalidate current source ownership, archive, revocation, and canonical contents under source row locks. Revocation after dispatch prevents a result from being accepted as completed. Completed result replay also rechecks access. Existing source attempts, responses, assignments, and authored Activities are never modified by these RPCs.\n+\n+## Executed isolated checks on 2026-10-01\n+\n+- `node scripts/verification/activity-ai-admission.mjs`: 103 PGlite SQL assertions passed. These exercise disabled configuration, ordinary role denial, source ownership, trusted snapshot fields and checklist, malformed/null source shapes, exact UUID conflicts, semantic aliases, quota and concurrency gates, claim rotation, nonrepeatable dispatch, ambiguous outcome retention, result validation/replay, attempt-two history proof, revocation/archive/source mutation, duplicate orders, and original-source preservation.\n+- `node scripts/verification/activity-ai-admission-real-pg.mjs`: 33 real PostgreSQL 17 race, role, and preservation assertions passed. Four concurrent matching admissions produce one reservation, four aliases, and one quota debit; four dispatches produce exactly one dispatch; concurrent finish produces one completion and three cached replays. Independent admissions respect three-request concurrency. Reclaim rotates exactly one claim; expired dispatched requests remain uncertain. Distinct actors racing global capacity admit exactly one. A real ordinary login cannot read private tables, call admission, or `SET ROLE` to service/installer. Functions belong to a non-superuser installer, and all five original source tables retain exact values.\n+\n+The retained real PostgreSQL proof database is `activity_ai_998e563a4f41` on the explicitly owned local cluster `127.0.0.1:55437`. No existing databases or fixtures were dropped. This is isolated validation, not deployed evidence.\n+\n+## Deployment gates and limits\n+\n+Before managed installation, independently review the SQL and Edge transport together, verify deployed `profiles.archived_at`, `activity_assignments.revoked_at`, canonical `profiles.class_id`, and assignment response column shapes, and take fresh source count/value snapshots. The earlier revocation SQL is a prerequisite even where migration history alone does not contain it. Install only through the confirmed Lovable Cloud route. Installation must leave the new configuration disabled and preserve every original source table, policy, and function definition.\n+\n+Activation is a separate explicit configuration action after the deployed RPC permissions and ordinary-JWT denials pass. A paid end-to-end Activity call still requires Joshua's immediate credit-spend confirmation. Mocked Edge tests and isolated SQL tests establish contract behavior, not model grading quality.\n+\n+The database cannot prove that a provider did or did not charge an ambiguous request. It never automatically reclaims such dispatches. Unknown outcomes can consume the actor's concurrency until their original claim reports a known result; no administrative resolution interface is part of this batch. Budget windows count admitted requests, not token costs. The broader tutoring, RRC, voice, and operator AI endpoints are outside this Activity-only contract.\n*** End Patch"));
